messages:
Jen Park: Quick sync — proposing a small concurrency sweep for queueing_v2. Idea: raise soft max_concurrency from 80 -> 100 but limit the audience to 10% initially (from 5%). Goal is to validate latency tail and queueing behavior before a wider rollout. Thoughts?
Samir Patel: +1 for validating tail latencies. Can we gate by region and customer tier? want to avoid hitting EU p95 if traffic spikes.
Leo Zhang: Agree. Suggest targeting non-enterprise customers in us-west/us-east only for the first 48h. Also added a small config snippet I tested locally: 
```
feature_flag: queueing_v2_concurrency_sweep
settings:
  audience_percent: 10
  audience_selector: "region:us*,tier:standard"
  soft_max_concurrency: 100
  rollback_if_p95_increase_pct: 25
  observation_window_minutes: 60
```
Maria Gonzales: Who's comfortable flipping the flag once PR is green? I can do the change in the console and monitor dashboards for the first hour.
Prashant Nair: Metrics to watch: p95 latency, queue length, token/sec per-worker, and alloc free GPU slots. I recommend alerts: p95 > baseline *1.25 for 15m OR queue length > 200 for 5m -> immediate rollback. I'll add those to the runbook.
Jen Park: Good call on alerts. I'll add the canary audience and the rollout note to the ticket (ENGPLAT-4821) and tag the docs. Maria — if you flip, please add a message in #eng-oncall and ping @Prashant.
OpsBot: PR #4512 merged by Leo Zhang — auto-deploy queued to canary. See: https://ci.internal/4512
Samir Patel: quick nit: make sure the policy falls back to concurrency 80 for dedicated customers (enterprises) so we don't break guaranteed capacity.
Leo Zhang: added that fallback in the flag rule (checked locally). The behavior: if customer.type == enterprise -> use soft_max_concurrency: 80, else the sweep applies.
Maria Gonzales: Flipped the flag in prod-canary at 2071231000. Monitoring now. Will report at 15/30/60m. :eyes:
Prashant Nair: Seeing a small p95 uptick (+8%) in us-west after 12m, queue length steady. No action yet, keep observing.
Jen Park: ok sounds healthy. If anything crosses the rollback thresholds, someone should revert and post a short postmortem note. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
